source.text: לָ/כֵ֤ן יָשׁ֣וּב עַמּ֣/וֹ הֲלֹ֑ם וּ/מֵ֥י מָ֝לֵ֗א יִמָּ֥צוּ לָֽ/מוֹ׀׃
source.note: WLC selected Masoretic reading form. Provisional selection of the explicitly recorded WLC/OSHB qere יָשׁ֣וּב, Qal imperfect 3ms, in place of written ישיב, tagged Hiphil imperfect 3ms. All other source words and punctuation are unchanged; upstream WLC XML is unchanged. This is a reading-tradition selection, not newly deciphered letters or settled earliest wording.

apparatus.note: Written alternative interpreted as causative: he brings his people back. The electronic ketiv is unpointed; יָשִׁיב is grammatical expansion, not fresh observed vocalization.

Selected provisionally: his people return. These related digital controls do not represent two independent manuscripts. Selected Greek and Syriac broadly support returning people but say my and diverge in the second clause; they do not establish exact Hebrew back-translation.

source.numbering_note: Hebrew/POB Psalm 73:10 aligns with Greek and selected Latin Psalm 72:10 by the full local sequence, not numbering alone.

translation.text: Therefore his people return here[a], and abundant waters are drained for them[b].

footnotes.text: The main text follows the Masoretic reading form, “his people return.” The written form is interpreted as “he brings his people back.” The referent of “his” and the location “here” remain uncertain. Selected Greek and Syriac say “my people”; they also differ in the following clause. Earliest wording remains unresolved.
Or “and abundant waters are drained by them.” The Hebrew expression is difficult, and the final pronoun may be understood as “for them” or “by them.”

lexical_decisions.rationale: Discourse marker indicating consequence from the preceding description of the wicked; 'Therefore' preserves the logical connection clearly in English.

lexical_decisions.lexicon: WLC/OSHB morphology and published GKC §72; no fresh HALOT consultation
lexical_decisions.rationale: Select the actual Qal qere HVqi3ms, not the written Hiphil-tagged ישיב. The singular collective עַמּוֹ naturally supplies the subject; English plural agreement does not change Hebrew morphology. Written causative support is preserved in the source apparatus and note. Historical priority is unresolved.
Straightforward construct with 3ms suffix. 'His people' preserves the ambiguity of the referent of 'his' in context rather than resolving it interpretively.
Adverb of place meaning 'here/to here.' 'Here' is idiomatic modern English and preserves the spatial sense.
Construct plural of 'water.' English often uses the mass noun 'water,' but 'waters' better reflects the Hebrew plural and poetic register.
Adjectival form 'full' modifies 'waters'; in English the idiom 'waters in abundance' communicates the sense more naturally than the wooden 'waters of fullness.'

Niphal of מצה carries the sense of being drained out or wrung out. 'Are drained' is the clearest modern English rendering, while preserving the passive sense. Because the image is difficult, an alternative is preserved in a footnote.

The preposition with pronominal suffix can be read in several ways here. With the passive verb, 'by them' yields a coherent sense ('waters ... are drained by them'). Because 'for them' is also possible and reflected in many translations, that alternative is preserved in a footnote.
This is idiomatic English and preserves both the water image and the idea of fullness or abundance.
The passive draining image is retained, and the lamed pronoun is naturally read as a dative; an agentive construal remains in the note.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Left ambiguous in the main text
theological_decisions.rationale: The Hebrew suffix does not explicitly identify the antecedent, and the verse is syntactically difficult. To avoid importing a doctrinal or interpretive resolution not demanded by the text, the translation preserves the ambiguity.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy §3: Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.

revisions.source_review: WLC Hebrew, chapter context, prior Sol/Terra proposal and final high-scrutiny adjudication
revisions.from: Therefore his people turn back here[a][b][c], and waters of fullness are drained by them.
revisions.to: Therefore he brings his people back here[a], and abundant waters are drained for them[b].
revisions.rationale: The prior adjudication best represents the formally causative ישיב and the ordinary dative force of לָמוֹ, while retaining the intransitive and agentive alternatives. “Abundant waters” is preferable to the unnatural “waters of fullness.” The only necessary further revision is proper footnote placement: marker [b] belongs immediately after the clause it qualifies and before the period.

revisions.from: Therefore he brings his people back here[a], and abundant waters are drained for them[b].
revisions.to: Therefore his people return here[a], and abundant waters are drained for them[b].
revisions.rationale: Explicitly select the attested Qal reading form instead of the written Hiphil-tagged form. Change the people from object of an unnamed causative agent to subject of return; preserve possessive/deictic ambiguity, written alternative and all second-clause wording. Prior model agreement is archived and does not approve this source.

source_audit.scope: One recorded Masoretic qere and corresponding first-clause English; the second clause is retained, not newly resolved.
